bypass_blocks_surface_label: Example bypass-blocks / skipnav posture for official voter-information routes
delivery_role_note: Bounded first-entry surface for official voter-information routes where repeated banner/header/navigation chrome appears before the answer-bearing main content.

repeated_blocks.block_label: Government banner + site header + primary navigation
repeated_blocks.materiality_note: A sequential user would otherwise traverse the same repeated chrome before every visit to the main answer lane.

primary_bypass_paths.entry_target_note: The bypass path lands at the start of the answer-bearing main content rather than above a decorative hero or another repeated control cluster.
primary_bypass_paths.mobile_variant_note: The same bypass mechanism remains available when the mobile menu button and government banner are present.
primary_bypass_paths.route_local_repeated_block_note: A route-local in-page navigation rail appears after main entry and therefore does not replace the top-level bypass path.

main_entry_target_note: The office reviewed whether the primary skip target is the real beginning of the current answer/help lane and not an empty wrapper or hidden element.
first_focusable_item_note: The first practical focus path offers a bounded jump into main content instead of forcing traversal through the full repeated header burden on each visit.
mobile_header_and_banner_note: Mobile headers, menu buttons, and the official banner were included in the repeated-block review because they materially affect first-entry burden.
route_local_repeated_block_note: Where a route contains additional repeated local navigation before the answer lane, the office records whether one top-of-page bypass remains sufficient or whether another bounded bypass was needed.
landmark_and_skipnav_interplay_note: Semantic landmarks support nonvisual navigation, but the route also preserves an ordinary sequential bypass path into main content.
